overview: This 299-page file brings together U.S. diplomatic and military intelligence assessments of Japanese communism during the Occupation, chiefly in 1948–49. Reports, correspondence, translations, and organizational indexes trace the Japan Communist Party’s electoral strategy, recruitment, labor activity, peace campaigns, and international ties. The file also documents American debate over the Communist threat and revisits Prince Konoe’s 1945 warning of revolution.
interest: Translated party documents sit beside U.S. assessments, revealing both Communist strategies and American interpretations of them.
